Your wallet just did a double-take. LEGO announced the Fantastic Four's robotic buddy, H.E.R.B.I.E., as a buildable figure, and while the price is a bit steep, the build itself looks surprisingly solid. We've seen impressive droids in the Star Wars line before, but this one aims for a similar scale, and frankly, it seems to nail the retro-futuristic vibe.

The 747-piece set, [76339](/sets/76339-the-fantastic-four-herbie) The Fantastic Four H.E.R.B.I.E., is designed to capture that classic look from "The Fantastic Four: First Steps." From what the review suggests, LEGO has done a commendable job with the proportions and the rounded shape, making it instantly recognizable. The head's sharp angles and the curved body are recreated using clever brickwork, with sections fitting together quite neatly. It's comparable in size to sets like the 75379 R2-D2, which means it’s substantial enough for display without taking up too much real estate on your shelf. This scale also opens up possibilities for other Marvel characters in the future – imagine a brick-built Thing!

Articulation is a key feature here, limited to the arms and neck, mirroring the character's on-screen presence. While not overly complex, these joints are enough to give H.E.R.B.I.E. a good range of expression, especially with the head's ability to tilt, making it look like it's listening or contemplating. The reviewer noted a slight wish for more inward shoulder movement, but it’s a minor point. The head design itself is a highlight, using clip plates for the hexagonal structure around the face and curved slopes for a smooth finish. The printed discs for eyes and the brick-built mouth details are excellent. A neat touch is the internal gears that turn the eyes when the head rotates, adding a subtle bit of animation to the model. The rubber tyre cleverly disguises the neck joint, allowing for that crucial head tilt, which is a rarity in these types of buildable figures.

While the back of the head is a bit plain compared to the film, the reviewer acknowledges that adding those details would likely have required stickers, which aren't included. All decorated parts on the front, including the Fantastic Four emblem on the chest, are printed – a huge win. The texture on the midriff is also well done. The designer has clearly worked with existing parts to achieve a great result, even if it’s not absolutely perfect. A clever feature is the removable panel on the front of the body, which hides storage for a couple of accessories. It's a well-integrated feature that doesn't disrupt the overall look.

However, the set isn't without its minor drawbacks. The reviewer points out that it's a "little overpriced," especially when compared to the piece count and the general market. While the build experience and the final model are strong, that price point might make some fans hesitate.

In India, the LEGO Fantastic Four H.E.R.B.I.E. (76339) is available at Toycra for ₹7,499. Use code ABHINAV12 for 12% off on orders above ₹500 at Toycra. That's enough for 10 months of Spotify Premium Family Plan. MyBrickHouse will likely stock it 4–6 weeks after global launch.

Overall, the LEGO Fantastic Four H.E.R.B.I.E. (76339) is a visually impressive buildable character that captures its source material well. The printing on decorated elements is a big plus, and the articulation, especially the head tilt, adds significant personality. The primary concern is the price, which feels a touch high for what you get. If you're a die-hard Fantastic Four fan or a collector of brick-built characters, it’s a strong contender. For others, waiting for a sale or a price drop might be the wiser move.

Your wallet is already feeling the heat. LEGO’s new Boba Fett statuette ([75455](/sets/75455-boba-fett)) stands a towering 41cm tall, promising serious display presence. But at this price point, it needs to be more than just big. It needs to be brilliant. Does it deliver on that iconic bounty hunter promise? Let's find out.

The box itself rocks the familiar 18+ black design, showcasing the finished model. Inside, you'll find 15 numbered bags of bricks, an instruction manual, and a sticker sheet. Speaking of stickers, it’s a bit disappointing to see the sticker sheet just floating around loose in the box. A little folder inside the manual would have protected it much better. Honestly, for a premium display piece like this, you expect a bit more care in packaging.

The build process is surprisingly engaging. It starts with the base, then moves to the legs, building them up section by section. The torso and arms follow, with a rather finicky rubber belt adding a touch of challenge. Finally, the head, jetpack, and accessories come together. The reviewer notes a unique building experience, focusing on textures and shaping. It’s not just a simple stack-and-build; there's some clever technique involved in bringing this statuette to life.

The set includes just one minifigure, but it’s a new, accurate Boba Fett for Episode VI. It matches the large-scale version well, with detailed prints and accessories. The main event, though, is the statuette itself. It’s a classy display piece, complete from all angles. Even the back is detailed, which is a nice touch for a set meant to be seen from every direction. The colour scheme is spot-on, mirroring the movie character and the included minifigure.

The helmet is where the designers really shine. Capturing those iconic lines at this scale, using a mix of prints, stickers, and brick-built elements, is impressive. The head swivels, and the rangefinder is adjustable. A cool easter egg inside the helmet features 1x1 studs representing Boba Fett’s concept art colours – a neat nod for dedicated fans.

However, the reviewer also points out the use of stickers for some key details, which might deter purists. The rubber belt attachment is described as finicky, and the overall weight of the model, while good for presence, means it's not something you'll be moving around constantly. The price is also a significant factor. While it’s a large and detailed model, the sticker use and the sheer cost mean it’s not an automatic buy for everyone.

In India, both MyBrickHouse and Toycra list the LEGO Boba Fett (75455) for ₹17,999. That's about enough to cover your monthly EMI for a decent mid-range smartphone or a very good haul of Indian sweets for a family gathering. MyBrickHouse and Toycra are the stores to watch — use code ABHINAV12 for 12% off on orders above ₹500 at Toycra.

Overall, the LEGO Boba Fett (75455) is a highly detailed and visually striking display piece. It captures the essence of the character well, with a satisfying build and some clever design choices. The inclusion of a new minifigure and the thoughtful details like the helmet easter egg add value. Yet, the sticker situation and the hefty price tag prevent it from being a universal recommendation. It's a premium product for dedicated Star Wars collectors who appreciate large-scale builds and can stomach the cost. For most, waiting for a sale or a price drop would be the sensible move.

Your wallet is probably already sweating. LEGO announced the [77254](/sets/77254-ferrari-sf90-xx-stradale-sports-car) Ferrari SF90 XX Stradale and it's landed in India with a price that feels… aspirational. It’s a Speed Champions set, which usually means a good time, but this Prancing Horse demands a serious look before you commit. Is this hypercar replica worth the price of admission?

The box itself is standard Speed Champions fare. A Ferrari red blur on the front, a track scene on the back. Inside, you'll find five numbered bags, the chassis, instructions, and a surprisingly small sticker sheet. For a Speed Champions set, that’s a good sign. Less fiddly stickers mean less room for error and a smoother build.

The build process, according to our reviewer, is where this set shines. It’s described as detailed, with enjoyable and innovative techniques. This isn't just slapping bricks together; it's a proper construction. The higher-than-average piece count for a set this size certainly helps in achieving that satisfying build experience. You start with the chassis and interior, then gradually build up the exterior, with the key details like the front section and rear wing taking shape around bag four. The final bag completes the model, leaving you with a sleek, accurate replica.

The minifigure included is a Ferrari driver, complete with a red Ferrari-branded hoodie. It’s a nice touch, especially for any Formula 1 fans looking to customise their own figures. The printed grey belt detail is a smart addition, though it does limit the hoodie’s versatility slightly. She comes with a helmet and a spanner, standard but welcome accessories.

Now, the finished model. The reviewer is clearly impressed. The iconic Ferrari red is present, accented with black. The unique front end of the real SF90 XX Stradale has been translated surprisingly well into LEGO form, thanks to some clever use of wedge plates and tiles at various angles. The introduction of a couple of new pieces, like tiled versions of 1x2 angled plates, really helps achieve that smooth, flowing look. The bonnet shaping is particularly praised, with upside-down black plates adding texture and tiny gaps mimicking the real car's hood scoops. It sounds like a masterclass in LEGO car design.

The side bodywork also benefits from new pieces, including a 1x1 inverted corner cheese slope and those aforementioned 1x2 angled tiles. The printed mudguards and 1x1 slope with the Ferrari logo are a delight – printed elements are always a win. And then there are the wheels. A stunning new wheel and tyre design that is described as "stunningly Ferrari-esque." The rear, while appearing simpler, packs in clever techniques for diffuser details and bodywork shaping. Even the trans-black rear window uses those new angled tiles effectively. Access to the interior is gained by detaching the windscreen, revealing a space for two minifigures, a steering wheel with a yellow centre (a nice detail!), and some stickered interior elements.

At ₹2,999, this is the price of 14 months of Spotify Premium.
MyBrickHouse and Toycra both have it for ₹2,999. Use code ABHINAV12 for 12% off on orders above ₹500 at Toycra.

The Verdict? This Ferrari SF90 XX Stradale is a strong contender in the Speed Champions line. The build experience is praised for its detail and innovation, the minifigure is a nice bonus, and the finished model is a visual treat with clever part usage and new elements. The price is a bit steep for Speed Champions, but the quality of the build and the accuracy of the final design justify it. If you’re a Ferrari fan, or just appreciate a well-designed LEGO car, this is one you’ll want to add to your collection. It’s a good build, looks fantastic, and the price, while not cheap, is fair for what you get.
